newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Sejm may vote on NFI tax break next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish Sejm may vote on NFI tax break next week.

text.p: Poland's Sejm, the lower house, may vote next week on a bill on investment funds, including a tax exemption on capital gains for National Investment Funds (NFIs), a parliamentary committee official said on Friday.
The vote on the bill, which creates a legal framework for all types of funds, was scheduled for this week.
But deputies decided on Tuesday to send the draft for further work to parliamentary committees which failed to get it ready for a final vote during this week's session.

"We have done everything to have the final reading during this week's session but we failed to do so and the vote is most likely to take place during the next session which starts next Tuesday," an official from the privatisation committee told Reuters.

In April the finance ministry announced that from the start of 1998 it would scrap a tax exemption for the 15 NFIs on gains made on sales of firms from their portfolios but later the investment funds draft was amended to extend the exemption.
The debate on the issue kept trade in NFI units volatile last month and expectations of a final decision on the issue have kept NFI trade active this week, traders said.
